phase3_findings.description: The wider require_base_tables duty for custom runners (refuse child tables, calls matching database-defined routines, failed catalog lookups) is enforced only by documentation; RlsGuardRunner.__init__ checks only the parameter name.
_refuse_database_routines treats every non-postgres dialect as MySQL; the postgres/mysql precondition is enforced only by its caller and is not stated in the function or docstring.
The PostgreSQL pg_class row is read by position (row[0], row[1:3], row[3]); the child-flag meaning depends on the SELECT list order. Fails closed today.

The _called_names docstring (and docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md line 45) says strpos is emitted as POSITION; the PR's own test comment says the rewrite emits STRPOS on sqlglot 25.x and POSITION on 30.x, and the project allows sqlglot>=25.0,<31.

Ambiguous sentence 'no collected name skips the query' in the internal RLS doc; the code skips the routine lookup when no name is collected. 'One parameterized query per statement' means per verify_base_tables call.

The verify_base_tables fail-closed handler now also catches routine-lookup and tokenizer failures but still logs and returns a message about a relation-type check; for a relation-free call the message names a check that never ran.

The routine check runs only for dialect postgres or mysql; for any other dialect a relation-free call passes unchecked, while _verify_relations raises RlsError for an unknown dialect. No shipped runner reaches this.

_called_names sends each name as written, lower-cased and ASCII-only lower-cased; no test pins all three spellings because _FakeCatalog lower-cases every parameter and connector tests use ASCII names only.
The changelog.d/325.security.md fragment required by acceptance criterion twelve is missing; the diff adds no changelog.d file.
test_untokenizable_or_unparsable_sql_fails_closed uses inputs that fail inside _relations before _called_names runs, so the _called_names tokenizer failure path is never reached by a test.

_FakeCatalog.execute dispatches with sql.startswith('SET ') and splits a qualified name with .split('.'), string handling the repository's sqlglot rule names (test fake over fixed catalog queries only).
